+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|          DIGITAL RHETORIC — LANDSCAPE                            |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  CORE AFFORDANCES (what the medium enables)                     |
|  Brevity (Twitter/X: 280 chars; headlines; notifications)       |
|  Virality (share/retweet/forward mechanics)                     |
|  Decontextualization (screenshots, clips separated from source) |
|  Asynchrony (delay between statement and response)              |
|  Anonymity and pseudonymity (authorship uncertainty)            |
|  Algorithmic curation (not all speech is heard equally)         |
|  Persistence (what is said is searchable and archived)          |
|  Multimodality (text + image + audio + video in sequence)       |
|                                                                  |
|  KEY PHENOMENA                                                   |
|  The meme as compressed argument                                 |
|  Algorithmic amplification and filter bubbles                   |
|  Platform-specific rhetorical genres                            |
|  Deepfakes and synthetic media as credibility attacks           |
|  Source credibility in an environment of abundant fakes         |
|                                                                  |
|  COMPUTING CONNECTION                                            |
|  Recommendation algorithms are not neutral; they optimize for   |
|  engagement, which correlates with emotional arousal.           |
|  The algorithm IS a rhetorical actor — it selects which         |
|  arguments reach which audiences.                               |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
